articles.title: What Is a Snowflake?
articles.dek: Snow is cold, soft and white. But how does a snowflake grow?

sources.name: Live Science: Why is snow white?

paras: It is a cold winter morning. You look out of the window, and everything is white. Snow! But what is snow, really? Where does it come from? And why is it white? Let's answer these questions one by one.

What is a snowflake? It is a small piece of ice. It starts high up in a cloud. Up there, the air is very cold. A tiny drop of water freezes onto a piece of dust or pollen. Now it is a very small ice crystal.

How does it get bigger? The crystal starts to fall slowly. On the way down, more water from the air freezes onto it. It grows arms, and it becomes a snowflake. If the air is cold all the way to the ground, the snowflake doesn't melt. It lands as snow.

How many sides does a snowflake have? Almost always six! Water makes this shape when it freezes. The weather changes the shape too. Some snowflakes look like flat stars. Others look like long, thin needles.

Why are no two snowflakes the same? Every snowflake takes a different way from the cloud to the ground. Each one meets a little more cold air or a little more water. So each one grows in its own special way.

Who took the first photo of a snowflake? His name was Wilson Bentley. He was a farmer in Vermont, in the USA. In 1885, he used a camera and a microscope to take the first photo. In his life, he took more than 5,000 photos of snow crystals. People called him 'Snowflake Bentley'.

And why is snow white? A single piece of ice is clear, like glass. But snow has millions of ice crystals and a lot of air between them. Light hits the crystals and bounces around many times. Then it comes back out to your eyes. All the colours of light together look white. Which answer was the most interesting for you?

articles.title: Zara's Song
articles.dek: Zara loves singing, but only alone in her bedroom. Then her teacher asks her to sing at the concert.
paras: Zara was twelve, and she loved music. She taught herself to play the guitar when she was ten. She often sang in her bedroom by herself. But she never sang in front of other people. Just thinking about it made her feel sick.

One Monday, her music teacher, Mr Kim, stopped her after class. 'Zara, I heard you in the music room at lunch,' he said. 'You have a lovely voice. Will you sing a song at the winter concert?' Zara looked at him. She wanted to say no, but she said yes.

For two weeks, she practised every evening. She stood in front of the mirror and watched herself. Her little brother, Sami, listened at the door. 'You're really good!' he told her. 'Thanks,' said Zara. 'But I'm still scared.'

On the night of the concert, the hall was full. Zara's parents were in the second row, and her best friend, Lily, was next to them. Zara walked onto the stage with her guitar. Her hands were shaking. She looked at all the faces, and she forgot the first words of the song!

For a moment, nobody moved. Then Lily stood up and smiled at her. She started to sing the first line quietly. Zara heard her, and the words came back. 'Come on, Zara, you can do it,' she told herself. She started again.
This time, everything was fine. Her voice was strong and clear. At the end, everyone clapped and cheered. Mr Kim gave her a big smile. Her parents were very proud of her.

After the concert, Zara found Lily outside. 'Thank you for helping me,' she said. 'You saved me!' Lily laughed. 'No, you did it yourself. I only sang one line!' That night, Zara said to herself, 'Maybe I'm not so shy after all.'

articles.title: Three Languages at Fourteen
articles.dek: Lucas speaks Spanish, English and a little Chinese. How does he do it?
paras: Lucas Moreno is fourteen and lives in Valencia, Spain. He speaks Spanish, English and a little Chinese. We asked him about learning languages.

Lucas, how did you start learning English? My mum is from Ireland, so she always spoke English to me at home. I understood it easily when I was small. But I spoke it badly at first! I often mixed up English and Spanish words.

Why did you choose Chinese? Two years ago, a new student called Mei came to my class. She was from Shanghai. She spoke Spanish slowly and carefully, and I wanted to help her. Then I thought, 'Why don't I learn her language too?'

Is Chinese difficult? Yes, very! The writing is hard. I write every character slowly, again and again. The tones are difficult too. If you say a word wrongly, it means something different. Once I wanted to say 'mum', but I said 'horse'! Mei laughed loudly.

How do you practise? I use an app for ten minutes every day. I also watch cartoons in Chinese. And every Friday, Mei and I meet at the library. For thirty minutes we speak Chinese, and then we speak Spanish. We both learn quickly that way.
What is your best tip? Don't be afraid of mistakes! Listen carefully and speak clearly. Learn a few new words every day. And be patient, because nobody learns a language in one week.
What's next for you? Next summer, I'm going to visit Mei's family in Shanghai. I want to speak to her grandparents, so I'm studying hard. I hope they understand me!
